# Body Scope

## How To Build

A BodyScope should be built as a reusable component that will be reused throughout the rest of the codebase.  A component is configurable through arguments or properties that alter its behaviour, appearance, and details.  A BodyScope should encapsulate all of its own reusable behaviour, while leaving the wiring, intergration, and integration to the domain of the application.

## Theme

Drawn in the [ThemeScope](../../ui/theme/index.md#theme-scope): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.

## Concept

### Pitch

The main window's body: the area between its two sidebars, where the tasks sent to the harness, and any file opened beside them, are shown.

### Shape

#### Description

Beneath the [RibbonScope](../../ui/components/ribbon/index.md#ribbon-scope) and above the [ChatInputScope](../prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope), between the [ProjectSidebarScope](../../ui/components/project-sidebar/index.md#project-sidebar-scope) on its left and, while a task runs, the [ReferencedSpecSidebarScope](../../ui/components/referenced-spec-sidebar/index.md#referenced-spec-sidebar-scope) on its right. While that sidebar isn't there, the body reaches the window's right edge. It is part of the [PromptEditor](../prompt-mode/index.md#prompt-editor), whose chat input runs beneath it and beneath the right sidebar, across the full width of prompt mode.

#### Contents

Everything that can be in the body:

- the [MessageList](../prompt-mode/message-list/index.md#message-list), the chat history, which fills it whenever no file is open
- the hint shown in the message list's place before any task has been sent, or while no project is open, as the [PromptEditor](../prompt-mode/index.md#prompt-editor) and the [NoProjectStateScope](../no-project/index.md#no-project-state-scope) say
- an [EditorScope](../editor/index.md#editor-scope), in a split beside the message list, while a file is open

An [InsetPanelScope](../../ui/components/inset-panel/index.md#inset-panel-scope) floats over the whole window, the body included, but is never part of it.

#### Open File

A file opened, from the [FileTreeScope](../../ui/components/file-tree/index.md#file-tree-scope) or anywhere else the [OpenFileScope](../open-file/index.md#open-file-scope) says, shows in an [EditorScope](../editor/index.md#editor-scope), in a split beside the chat history: the file on the left taking 50% of the width, the chat history on the right taking the rest. The split can be resized by dragging its edge. Closing the file closes the split.
When the split opens, it slides in from the sidebar, so it's clear where it came from: the file's side grows out of the sidebar's edge to its share of the width, the file sliding into view from behind that edge as it does, over the chat history. The chat history keeps its width while the file slides over it, so nothing in it is laid out anew each frame, and takes the rest of the width once the slide settles.
The slide is quick and settles without bouncing, and only then can the split be dragged. A file opened in place of one already showing doesn't slide, since the split is already open. The [ChatInputScope](../prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope) is never split: it stays along the bottom, across the full width of prompt mode.
Closing the file plays the slide in reverse, back into the

##### Sidebar

the file's side shrinks from whatever width it was

dragged to down to nothing at the sidebar's edge, the file sliding out of view behind that edge as it does, uncovering the chat history, which is back across the full width beneath it from the start of the slide. It is as quick as the slide in, and settles without bouncing. Opening a file while one is still sliding out slides the new one in straight away.

content.text:
The app already places the chat input that way, so this doesn't change the fix.

In the screenshot I took before editing, the chat input starts right at the left sidebar's edge and stretches under the task list and the Referenced Spec sidebar to the window's right edge. The left sidebar runs the full height beside it. That matches the Body spec: the chat input sits below the body and the right sidebar, across the full width of prompt mode, and is never split. My changes only touch the layout inside the chat input (the text box and its button column), so they don't move its outer edges.

I added this placement as a constraint in the understanding file. I haven't checked the fix in the running app yet, because my screenshot afterwards caught a different window.
